_doc: One entry per case file. `anchors` are substrings that each appear on exactly one line of the case; a finding counts as catching the seeded bug when its line is within `tolerance` lines of any anchor line. `bug: null` marks a clean control: no seeded bug, used to count false positives. run.py checks every anchor resolves to exactly one line before running anything.

01-paginate.js.bug: slice() end is exclusive, so `end = start + pageSize - 1` drops the last item of every page.

02-user_search.py.bug: name_prefix is interpolated into the SQL string with an f-string instead of being bound as a parameter.

03-notes-router.ts.bug: PUT /notes/:id never checks note.ownerId against req.user.id (GET does), so any signed-in user can overwrite anyone's note.

04-wallet.py.bug: Read-check-write on the balance with no row lock (with_for_update) or atomic update: concurrent withdrawals can both pass the check and overdraw.

05-sync-contacts.js.bug: forEach does not await async callbacks: the function returns 0 before any upsert finishes, and upsert errors become unhandled rejections.

06-export_reports.py.bug: The file is opened before the empty-rows check, so `continue` leaks the handle (and leaves an empty file); any exception while writing leaks it too — no `with` block.

07-discount.ts.bug: The spec says 65 or older, but `age > 65` excludes customers who are exactly 65.

08-analytics_events.py.bug: `tags: list[str] = []` is shared across calls and mutated by append, so every default-tagged event accumulates more `source:web` tags (and the caller's list is mutated too).
anchors: def build_event(name: str, payload: dict, tags: list[str] = []) -> dict:

09-auth-middleware.js.bug: jwt.decode() does not verify the signature; anyone can forge a token. SECRET is loaded but never used — this must be jwt.verify(token, SECRET).

10-job_progress.py.bug: Integer division happens before multiplying by 100, so any unfinished job reports 0%.

11-capture-order.ts.bug: A failed payment capture is only logged; execution continues and the order is marked paid and sent to fulfillment without the money being captured.
anchors: await orders.update(orderId, { status: "paid", paidAt: new Date() });

12-downloads.py.bug: filename comes from the URL (<path:...> allows slashes) and is joined without normalizing or checking it stays inside user_dir, so ../ reads other users' files or any file; an absolute path also discards user_dir entirely.

13-settings-tabs.js.bug: `var i` is function-scoped: every click handler sees the final i (tabs.length), so panels[i] is undefined and clicking throws.

14-ttl_cache.py.bug: Deleting from the dict while iterating over .items() raises RuntimeError (dictionary changed size during iteration) as soon as an entry has expired.

15-shipping-label.ts.bug: address is optional (new accounts lack it) but the non-null assertion destructures it unconditionally — TypeError at runtime for new accounts.

16-cors.js.bug: endsWith("example.com") also matches attacker origins like https://evil-example.com, and credentials are allowed, so a malicious site can make credentialed cross-origin reads.
